title: Set 167

sentences.ko: 네가 말해 준 그 라멘집 드디어 가 봤는데, 솔직히 왜 좋다는지 모르겠어. 아니, 괜찮긴 했는데 한 그릇에 25달러인 줄 알았으면 그냥 집에서 끓여 먹었을 거야.
sentences.text: I finally went to that ramen place you told me about, and honestly, I don't get it. Like, it was fine, but if I'd known it was going to be twenty-five bucks a bowl, I would've just made some at home.

alts.text: Tried that ramen spot you told me about, and honestly? Don't get it. It was fine, but if I'd known it was twenty-five bucks a bowl, I'd have just made some at home.

I finally visited the ramen restaurant you recommended, and to be honest, I do not understand the appeal. It was perfectly acceptable, but had I known it would cost twenty-five dollars a bowl, I would simply have made some at home.

sentences.note: **I don't get it** 은 남들이 좋다는데 나는 왜 좋은지 모르겠다고 할 때 씁니다. **bucks** 는 달러를 편하게 부르는 말입니다.
sentences.situation: 친구가 추천한 식당 다녀와서 후기 말하기

sentences.ko: 위층 남자가 밤 11시쯤에 운동을 하기 시작했는데, 꼭 내 천장 바로 위에 아령을 떨어뜨리는 소리가 나. 올라가서 한마디 해야지 계속 생각하는데, 유난 떠는 이웃은 되기 싫잖아.
sentences.text: The guy upstairs has started working out at like eleven at night, and it sounds like he's dropping the weights right on my ceiling. I keep thinking I should go up there and say something, but I don't want to be that neighbor, you know?

alts.text: Dude upstairs started working out around eleven at night, and it's like he's dropping the weights right on my ceiling. I keep thinking I should go up and say something, but I don't wanna be that neighbor, y'know?

The gentleman who lives upstairs has begun exercising at around eleven in the evening, and it sounds as though he is dropping the weights directly onto my ceiling. I keep meaning to go upstairs and speak with him, but I would rather not be that kind of neighbor.

sentences.note: **be that neighbor** 는 다들 피하고 싶어하는 그런 귀찮은 이웃이 된다는 뜻입니다. that 에 힘을 주어 말합니다.

sentences.ko: 훨씬 넓은 집을 찾았는데 한 달에 200달러밖에 더 안 들어. 근데 그러면 출퇴근이 편도로 거의 한 시간이야. 그래서 계속 마음이 왔다 갔다 해. 드디어 책상 놓을 자리가 생기긴 하는데, 거의 기차에서 살게 될 거거든.
sentences.text: We found a place that's way bigger and it's only two hundred more a month, but then my commute would be almost an hour each way. So I keep going back and forth, because I'd finally have room for a desk, but I'd basically be living on the train.

alts.text: Found a way bigger place, only two hundred more a month, but my commute'd be almost an hour each way. So I'm kinda torn. I'd finally have room for a desk, but I'd basically live on the train.

We have found a considerably larger apartment for only two hundred dollars more per month; however, my commute would be nearly an hour in each direction. I remain undecided, because I would finally have room for a desk, but I would essentially be living on the train.

sentences.note: **go back and forth** 는 이쪽저쪽 마음이 계속 바뀌며 못 정하는 것입니다. **each way** 는 편도로, 한 번 가는 데 걸리는 것을 말합니다.

sentences.ko: 자꾸 새벽 3시쯤에 깨는데, 그러고 나면 그날 했던 바보 같은 말들을 하나하나 곱씹으면서 그냥 누워 있어. 겨우 다시 잠들 때쯤이면 벌써 일어날 시간이 다 돼 있어.
sentences.text: I keep waking up at like three in the morning, and then I just lie there thinking about every dumb thing I said that day. By the time I finally fall back asleep, it's almost time to get up.

alts.text: Keep waking up around three a.m., and then I'm just lying there replaying every dumb thing I said that day. By the time I'm back asleep, it's pretty much time to get up.
I have been waking up at around three in the morning, and I then lie awake reflecting on every foolish thing I said that day. By the time I finally fall asleep again, it is nearly time to get up.

sentences.note: **lie there** 는 잠 못 들고 그냥 누워만 있는 모습입니다. **fall back asleep** 은 깼다가 다시 잠드는 것입니다.

sentences.ko: 그러니까 여행은 아직 갈 수 있는데, 그 다음 주에 가야 돼. 그 주말에 동생이 이사를 해서 도와주겠다고 이미 말해 놨거든. 너도 그때 괜찮아? 아니면 벌써 호텔 예약했어?
sentences.text: So I can still do the trip, but only if we go the week after, because my brother's moving that weekend and I already said I'd help him. Would that still work for you, or did you already book the hotel?

alts.text: I can still do the trip, but only the week after. My brother's moving that weekend and I already said I'd help. That still work for you, or did you book the hotel already?

I am still able to join the trip, but only if we go the following week, as my brother is moving that weekend and I have already promised to help him. Would that still be convenient for you, or have you already reserved the hotel?

sentences.note: **Would that still work for you?** 는 일정을 바꿀 때 상대에게도 괜찮은지 묻는 말입니다. **I can still do the trip** 의 do 는 여행에 같이 간다는 뜻으로 편하게 씁니다.

reviewed: 3번 한국어 '계속 왔다 갔다 해'는 몸이 오가는 것으로 읽혀 'go back and forth'의 뜻(마음이 왔다 갔다)이 안 살아남. '계속 마음이 왔다 갔다 해'로 고침
3번 formal 'two hundred more per month'에 단위가 빠져 격식체로는 어색함. 'two hundred dollars more per month'로 고침
2번 formal 'I continue to think that I ought to'는 원어민이 쓰지 않는 번역체임. 'I keep meaning to'로 바꾸고, 'a difficult neighbor'는 원문의 that neighbor 느낌을 살려 'that kind of neighbor'로 고침
4번 formal 'I have repeatedly been waking'은 부자연스러움. 'I keep waking up'의 격식체로 'I have been waking up'으로 고침
5번 한국어 '그 다음 주에 가는 경우에만 돼'가 딱딱한 번역투임. '그 다음 주에 가야 돼'로 고침
